narrative: Material PL3__MC6DA11C exhibits a smooth-intermittent demand pattern (CV=0.31, ~79% active days) with no statistically significant trend over the 228-day observation window. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.52, range 0.80–3.43 days), making continuous-review essential to guard against stockout risk. The EOQ-aligned order quantity of 21,996 units (well above the 5,682 MOQ) reduces annual ordering frequency from ~58 to ~15 orders, cutting ordering cost by 74%. A safety stock of 1,824 units is introduced to absorb the combined demand and lead-time variability at the 95% service level.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is approximately continuous with moderate variability (CV=0.31) and ~79% non-zero days, making a fixed-reorder-point / fixed-quantity policy appropriate. The high lead-time variability (CV=0.52) favours continuous over periodic review to react promptly to stock depletion.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is non-binding: safety_stock (1,824) + order_quantity (21,996) = 23,820 units, well below max_storage_units (45,440). No capacity-driven order reduction required.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None. MOQ (5,682) + safety_stock (1,824) = 7,506, which is feasible within max_storage_units (45,440).
